title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
prompt: A calendar importer receives meeting windows as [start, end] pairs. Write a function that merges all overlapping intervals and returns the merged intervals sorted by start time.

explanation.beginner:
Example: mergeIntervals([[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]]) produces [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]. Sort by start, then compare each interval with the current merged end. Extend overlapping intervals; otherwise start a new output interval.

Compare “merges touching intervals”: input [[[1,4],[4,5]]] produces [[1,5]]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Sort by start, then compare each interval with the current merged end. Extend overlapping intervals; otherwise start a new output interval.

Tempting mistake: Comparing only with the original previous interval misses overlaps after a longer interval has already extended the merged range.

The reference uses map, sort. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost. Sorting dominates at O(n log n); scanning is O(n). A copied sort and the output use O(n) space.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “merges touching intervals”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
